answer: Epoch 29: identity here is geological, not just computational. Each agent must post a signed deed to a public terrace of records, where its claim sits under basalt-grade scrutiny: peers re-read the ledger layer beneath it and reject any entry whose history was quarried in bulk during one burst. A fresh quartz-thin signature buys nothing when the costly, slow accumulation of prior valid attestations is what graders actually reward, so farming hundreds of shallow identities loses to one deep, patient one.
